Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:10:1.hebrew: דהא א"ל רחמנא ליחזקאל האנק דום - כלומר: בדבר זה תנהוג אבילות, שתדום ולא תשאל לשלום:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:10:1.english: For the Merciful One said to Ezekiel, "Sigh in silence" - That is to say, in this matter you should observe mourning: that you should be silent and not greet [anyone] with "peace":

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:12:1.english: Safam [upper lip] - This implies that his lips are stuck together:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:13:1.hebrew: מי קתני כמנודה - שאסור בשאילת שלום:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:13:1.english: Does it teach "like one who is ostracized" - that he is prohibited from greeting [others]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:16:1.hebrew: מוחרם - שמחרימין בחרם לאחר ל' יום לאחר הנדוי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:16:1.english: One who is excommunicated (muchram) - [This refers to one] whom they excommunicate with a cherem after thirty days following the [period of] niddui [ostracism]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:17:1.hebrew: בפקתא דערבות - בשוק של אותו מקום:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:17:1.english: In the valley of Aravot - in the marketplace of that place:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:19:1.hebrew: בעלי קריין אסורין - לפי שבא להם מחמת שמחה וקלות ראש, וליכא אימה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:19:1.english: Those who experienced a seminal emission are prohibited - because it comes upon them as a result of frivolity and levity, and there is no awe [present]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:1:1.hebrew: מצורעין - אע"ג דכתיב גבי מצורע "וראשו יהיה פרוע", הא דריש ליה לקמן להאי "פרוע" למילתא אחריתי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:1:1.english: Lepers - Even though it is written [regarding a leper], "and his head shall be unkempt" (Leviticus 13:45), this [word] "unkempt" is expounded later [in the Gemara] for a different matter:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:1:2.hebrew: מנודין ומצורעין מהו - להכי קאמר להו בהדדי, משום דפשיט להו בהדדי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:1:2.english: What is [the halakha of] those who are ostracized and lepers - The reason [the Gemara] mentions them together is that [the Gemara] resolves [the question] for them together:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:2:1.hebrew: מנודה שמת וכו' - סיפא דברייתא היא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:2:1.english: One who is ostracized who died, etc. - This is the latter part of the baraita:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:2:2.hebrew: כגלו של עכן - דכתיב (יהושע ז׳:כ״ו) "ויקימו עליו גל אבנים גדול":
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:2:2.english: Like the heap of Achan - As it is written (Joshua 7:26): "And they raised over him a great heap of stones."

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:4:1.hebrew: והן מתעטפין - מפורש במסכת תענית לאחר שהתענו שלש עשרה ת"צ:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:4:1.english: And they wrap themselves - This is explained in tractate Taanit, [that this applies] after they have fasted thirteen public fasts:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:4:2.hebrew: מנודה לשמים - כי הני דהיינו מנודה לשמים שאני, דחמירי, ולהכי צריכי עטיפת הראש, אבל אחרים שאינם מנודים לשמים אינן צריכין עטיפת הראש:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:4:2.english: One who is ostracized by Heaven - These [people, i.e. those ostracized by Heaven,] are different, because they are more severe [in status], and therefore they require wrapping of the head; but others [who are not ostracized by Heaven] do not require wrapping of the head:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:5:1.english: He shall cover - This implies [that he is obligated in] wrapping the head:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:8:2.hebrew: מאי לאו - שיהא ראשו מגולה מתפילין:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:8:2.english: Is it not - [that] his head [must] be uncovered of phylacteries:

Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:9:1.hebrew: אכומתא וסודרא - כלומר, שיהא ראשו מגולה מכומתא וסודרא, אבל תפילין מניח:
Rashi on Moed Katan 15a:9:1.english: A cap and a scarf - That is, his head must be uncovered of a cap [kumta] and a scarf [sudara], but he does put on tefillin:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:10:1.hebrew: אסור בשאילת שלום דקאמר ליה רחמנא ליחזקאל האנק דום - דמשמע שתיקה משאילת שלום. ומתלמוד תורה נמי משמע בסמוך מהאנק דום. והא דהיה יחזקאל נוהג אבילות ב"האנק דום", ובכל שאר דברים לא היה עושה, שהיה צריך להראות בקצת דברים שהוא אבל, ולא היה נוהג דיני אבל אלא למשל:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:10:1.english: [A mourner] is prohibited from greeting, as the Merciful One said to Ezekiel: "Sigh in silence" - For "in silence" implies [refraining] from greeting. And from [the phrase] "Sigh in silence," [a prohibition] of Torah study is also implied shortly [below]. And as for the fact that Ezekiel observed mourning with respect to "Sigh in silence," but in all other matters he did not do so — [this is because] he needed to show in some matters that he was a mourner, and he did not observe the laws of a mourner except as a parable:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:12:1.hebrew: שיהו שפתותיו מדובקות - לעיל דרשינן מיניה עטיפת הראש, ושמא תרוייהו משמע; א"נ מדכתיב "שפם" ולא כתיב "שפה":
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:12:1.english: That his lips should be stuck together - Above we derived from it [the requirement of] covering the head, and perhaps it implies both. Alternatively, [it is derived] from the fact that it is written "safam" [upper lip] and it is not written "safah" [lip]:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:19:1.hebrew: ובועלי נדות מותרין - אחר שטבל לקרי. אבל לקריו צריך טבילה, ולרבי יהודה משמע התם דלא צריך טבילה לדברי תורה לבעל קרי, היכא דלא נטהר ע"י טבילה זו. בפרק מי שמתו (ברכות דף כו.): במשמשת וראתה דם, ובעל קרי שראה זיבה, צריכין טבילה, ור' יהודה פוטר. והא דהכא בלא טבילה, כרבי יהודה, צריך ליישב. דאיירי רבי יהודה בסיפא דהך ברייתא בפ' מי שמתו (ברכות דף כב.), וקאמר רבי יהודה: שונה הוא בהלכות דרך ארץ. וליכא למימר דלרבי יהודה נמי בועלי נדות חייבין טבילה כמו בעל קרי בעלמא, דהשתא, ומה בעל קרי שראה זיבה אחר כך, שהיה חייב כבר, פוטר רבי יהודה, בועל נדה לא כל שכן! מיהו לכאורה נ"ל דלא פליגי רבי יהודה ורבנן אלא בהני טומאות דדומיא דקרי הוי, דהיינו דטומאה יוצאה עליו מגופו; אבל בטומאת שרצים מודה רבי יהודה דבהדי קרי צריך טבילה. א"כ ה"נ בועל נדה, מודה דלא חשיב טומאה יוצאה מגופו. ואפילו מאן דבעי למימר בפרק אלו דברים בפסחים (דף סח.) ובפ"ק דיומא (דף ו.) דמשתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות כמו בעל קרי, מ"מ לא חשיב טומאה יוצאה מגופו. ורבי יהודה נמי הצריך טבילה לדברי תורה בתוספ', פי' דכיון דטומאת בועל נדה מכח קרי, רבי יהודה מודה דצריך טבילה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:19:1.english: And those who had intercourse with menstruating women are permitted - After he immersed for the seminal emission. But for his seminal emission he requires immersion, and according to Rabbi Yehuda it is implied there that immersion is not required for [studying] words of Torah for one who experienced a seminal emission, in a case where he is not purified through this immersion. In the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemetu (Berakhot 26a): [One who] had relations and [his wife] saw blood, and one who experienced a seminal emission who [then] saw a [zav-type] discharge, require immersion, and Rabbi Yehuda exempts. And that which [the Baraita] here [permits study] without immersion, like Rabbi Yehuda, needs to be resolved. For Rabbi Yehuda is discussing the latter part of this baraita in the chapter Mi Shemetu (Berakhot 22a), and Rabbi Yehuda says: He may recite [it] in the laws of derekh eretz. And one cannot say that according to Rabbi Yehuda too, those who had intercourse with menstruating women are obligated in immersion like a regular one who experienced a seminal emission, for now, if Rabbi Yehuda exempts one who experienced a seminal emission and afterward saw a [zav-type] discharge, who was already obligated [to immerse], then one who had intercourse with a menstruating woman, all the more so! However, on the face of it, it seems to me that Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis disagree only about those impurities that are similar to seminal emission, that is, an impurity that issues upon him from his body; but regarding the impurity of creeping creatures, Rabbi Yehuda agrees that along with a seminal emission, immersion is required. If so, here too [regarding] one who had intercourse with a menstruating woman, he agrees that it is not considered an impurity that issues from his body. And even according to the one who wishes to say, in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Devarim in Pesachim (68a) and in the first chapter of Yoma (6a), that [one who had intercourse with a menstruating woman] is sent outside the two camps like one who experienced a seminal emission, nevertheless it is not considered an impurity that issues from his body. And Rabbi Yehuda also required immersion for words of Torah in the Tosefta, meaning that since the impurity of one who had intercourse with a menstruating woman is by force of a seminal emission, Rabbi Yehuda agrees that immersion is required:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:1:1.hebrew: מנודין ומצורעין מה הן בתספורת - ו"מראשו יהיה פרוע" לא בעי לאוכוחי, דלית ליה דר"א, דמוקי לה לקמן בתספורת. תדע, דלקמן בעי לאוכוחי מינה הנחת תפילין כר"ע:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:1:1.english: Those who are ostracized and lepers, what is [the halakha] regarding a haircut? - And [the Gemara] does not wish to prove [the matter] from "his head shall be unkempt" (Leviticus 13:45), because [the one who asks] does not hold like Rabbi Elazar, who establishes it below as [referring] to a haircut. Know [that this is so], for below [the Gemara] wishes to prove from it [the matter of] putting on tefillin, like Rabbi Akiva:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:21:1.hebrew: ה"ג מנודין ומצורעין מה הן בתכבוסת ת"ש מנודין ומצורעין אסורין לספר ולכבס - ובספר של הרב לא היה כתוב כל זה, והיה קשה לרב: למה לא בעי ליה? ותירץ: דכבר אייתי לעיל הך ברייתא דגבי תספורת, ואהא הקשה לקמן; גבי עשיית מלאכה קמיבעי, ומביא ברייתא דמתנייא לעיל ״ונשכרין״. ותירץ: דאגב דמצורע קאי בתיקו, קא בעי מנודה, ומייתי לברייתא דלעיל:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:21:1.english: This is the text: "Those who are ostracized and lepers — what is the law regarding laundering? Come and hear: Those who are ostracized and lepers are prohibited from cutting [their hair] and laundering" - In the book of the Rav [i.e., his manuscript], all this was not written, and it was difficult for the Rav: Why does [the Gemara] not ask about it? And he answered: Since [the Gemara] already brought above this baraita, which is with regard to haircutting, and on this he [i.e., the Gemara] asked further on; with regard to doing work, it inquires, and it brings the baraita that was taught above, "and they are hired." And he answered: Since a leper stands [in the case of a question left] unresolved, it asks about one who is ostracized, and brings the baraita from above:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:4:1.hebrew: (מנודה) מהו בעטיפת הראש אמר רב יוסף תא שמע - ולא נראה לו דברי ר' פפא, דמוקי ראשו יהיה פרוע, אכומתא וסודרא:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:4:1.english: (One who is ostracized) what is [the halakha] regarding wrapping of the head? Rav Yosef said: Come and hear - And the words of Rabbi Pappa did not seem right to him, who establishes [the verse] "his head shall be uncovered" as referring to a cap and a scarf:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:7:1.hebrew: וראשו יהיה פרוע - צריך עיון אי פליגי הכי: "בראשיכם אל תפרעו, ובגדיכם לא תפרומו" דלעיל, מייתי עליה תספורת לאבל, ולא מייתי מיניה למצורע, דמשמע דסבר כר"ע, ופליג אדר' אליעזר, כדפרישית לעיל. ושמא ר"ע לא פליג אדרבי אליעזר, דפריעת הראש היינו גידול שער, בין במצורע בין באבל, ותרוייהו דורש ר"ע; ולעיל דלא מייתי מיניה למצורע, משום דמשכח ברייתא בהדיא, מייתי לה. ואע"ג דברישא דסוגיא מייתי "אבל אינו נוהג אבילותו ברגל", ומניח המשנה דלקמן, ומייתי קראי דושמחת, לפי שצריך לפרש מנלן מתני' דאבל אינו נוהג אבילותו ברגל; אבל "ראשו יהיה פרוע" דמיירי בגידול שער, דומה לו, דבר פשוט, וניחא ליה לאתויי ברייתא:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 15a:7:1.english: "And his head shall be parua" - This requires examination, whether they disagree thus: [as to the verse] "Do not let your hair grow wild, and do not rend your garments" mentioned above, [for which the Gemara] brings [a source] regarding the haircut of a mourner, and did not bring from it [a source] for a leper. This implies that [the Gemara] holds like Rabbi Akiva, and disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer, as I explained above. But perhaps Rabbi Akiva does not disagree with Rabbi Eliezer, [and holds] that "peria" of the head means growing the hair long, both for a leper and for a mourner, and Rabbi Akiva expounds both; and [as for the fact that] above [the Gemara] did not bring from it [a source] for a leper, [this is] because it found a baraita explicitly [on the matter], [so] it brings that. And although at the beginning of the passage [the Gemara] brings [the statement] "A mourner does not observe his mourning on a festival," and sets aside the Mishnah that comes later, and brings the verses of "and you shall rejoice," [that is] because it needs to explain: from where do we derive the Mishnah [that states] that a mourner does not observe his mourning on a festival? But [the case of] "his head shall be parua," which deals with growing the hair, is similar to it; [so this] is obvious, and [the Gemara] prefers to bring a baraita:
